Dionysius the Elder

[Tyrant of Syracuse; born about 430 
B.C.;
 appointed one of the generals against the Carthaginians, and persuaded the people to intrust him with the government; died 367.]
I would have somebody more hated than myself.
When blamed for rewarding a wicked man, who was hated by the citizens.
In reply to the question, if he were at leisure, “God forbid,” he said, “that it should ever befall me!”
